Package names, extensions, drivers, and interfaces may change with rolling updates. All commands below are examples for reading; they were not executed or verified as part of this task.

The desktop installation commands assume that the base system boots and has network access. Third-party repositories, the AUR, and Flatpak are separate trust sources. Check package availability, verify signatures and authorization, then choose according to your needs. After enabling a repository, perform a full system upgrade; avoid installing packages with -Sy alone.

If native GNOME Wayland applications use the compositor's input protocol, do not unconditionally export GTK_IM_MODULE=fcitx globally. Follow Fcitx5's session instructions. When setting variables for specific applications such as WPS, prefer user-level launchers or wrapper scripts instead of directly modifying package-managed files such as /usr/bin/wps. Choose either IBus or Fcitx5 as the main input-method framework, and review environment variables and autostart entries when switching.

AppImage is a portable application format. Some Type 2 AppImages require the FUSE 2 compatibility library; they can also be extracted and run according to the project's instructions. Verify the source and execution permissions. Requiring no installation does not mean requiring no dependencies.
Install appimagelauncher to Manage AppImage Applications

After installation, launching an AppImage opens an appimagelauncher window. On first launch, it asks you to choose an installation path, defaulting to the Applications directory under your home directory. You can then choose to run it once or integrate it into the system. Installation sometimes fails, or the application may not run afterward.

To uninstall an AppImage application, right-click its shortcut and choose remove appimage from system. Alternatively, manually delete its desktop file from ~/.local/share/applications and its AppImage file from the installation directory.

Snapshots are convenient for saving system state, but they are not independent backups. Use the snapshot manager's deletion feature and keep an eye on disk space; there is no basis for assuming that bulk deletion inevitably crashes the system. Choose Timeshift, Snapper, and boot-menu integration approaches that match your subvolume layout.
